$comment: Machine-readable FRAMEWORK_CONTRACT (plan step S39). The contract was prose, and the conformance checker carried its own copy of every constant in it — the error taxonomy, the health shape, the nucleus tri-state, the OpenAPI path. Two sources of truth for one contract, free to drift, with nothing comparing them. This file is the single source; `runner/contract.mjs` reads it instead of hardcoding, and `runner/validate-ir.mjs` re-parses FRAMEWORK_CONTRACT.md and fails if the prose and this file disagree. Derived from the document 2026-08-16, not hand-typed.

health.$note: `nucleus` is the HEALTH of the dependency, NOT whether the database is a Nucleus instance. The contract says so explicitly: 'Feature detection (is the connected DB a Nucleus instance vs plain Postgres) is §1, not /health.' Elixir returned a boolean from is_nucleus?/1 here until 2026-08-16 — wrong type and wrong question — and its own test asserted the boolean.

featureDetection.$note: Whether the connected database is Nucleus vs plain PostgreSQL. Determined by parsing the version string for 'Nucleus'. Deliberately NOT the /health nucleus field.

errors.$probeNote: `validation` has no forced-error probe path on purpose: it is produced by POSTing an invalid body to the validation endpoint, and is asserted by the `validation.format` dimension instead. Every other code gets a GET endpoint that forces it. The checker used to hardcode a 7-entry list that silently omitted 422; here the omission is explicit and the count is checked against the document's 8-row table.

middleware.$note: Order is outermost-first and the contract says SHOULD, not MUST. Recorded so a framework's actual pipeline can be compared against it; today only the observable layers (request id, CORS, compression) are asserted over HTTP.

dimensions.asserts: status/version are strings; nucleus is one of the tri-state values
forced errors carry the RFC 7807 required fields
forced errors are served as application/problem+json
each taxonomy entry returns its status, type suffix and title
an invalid body returns 422 with a populated errors[]
the nucleus field reports dependency health, not DB identity
